prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: low-speed head-on collision in Baytown, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported neck and back strain. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1059; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was traveling in the eastbound lane when the vehicle collided head-on with Driver 2's vehicle at low speed. Officers arrived to find both vehicles stopped in the roadway with front-end damage consistent with the impact described by both drivers. Driver 2 stated that the collision occurred as Driver 1 reported, and two independent witnesses gave matching accounts of the sequence. Scene photographs taken by officers show damage patterns that align with the reported force of the impact. Driver 1 and a Passenger were both seated in the vehicle at the time, and officers and witnesses confirmed their presence. No prior damage to either vehicle was observed or reported. Driver 1 is listed as the named insured on the policy covering the vehicle. Driver 1 complained of neck and back discomfort at the scene and was transported for evaluation. The injuries described are consistent with the mechanics of a collision of this type and severity.
